title: The Dashboard demo hand-rolls a Legend, skips ChartFrame, and fixes its charts at 460px
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, asked to assess whether the patterns had drifted from the design system

evidence.verified: `npx vitest run src/patterns/`: 9 tests pass, four of them new. Reverting `DashboardDemo.tsx` fails all four, and the geometry one fails with `expected 477 to be less than or equal to 431`, which is 46px of the widest chart outside its card at a 430px viewport. With the fix the demo renders three `[data-component="Legend"]` roots carrying 12 `data-legend-swatch` and 12 `data-legend-label` hooks, and clearing the filter reaches `chartframe-empty` with the message the bespoke div used to hold. The four dashboard captures were re-recorded and read in both themes, and `npm run ci` exits 0 at 104/104 with 0 differing pixels.

details:
Three separate departures in one file.

It defines a local `Legend` component and uses it three times. The kit exports one, with a `shape` option, `role="group"` and documented `data-legend-swatch` and `data-legend-label` hooks. The local copy has none of that, and it passes resolved colours through `style={{ backgroundColor }}`, which is the one thing `components/Legend.md` forbids: swatch colours are custom-property names, never resolved values.

Its three charts sit in bare Cards. `patterns/Chart.md` says to wrap every chart in `ChartFrame`, so their empty branch is a bespoke div instead of the canonical empty block.

Each chart is a fixed 460 by H pixel SVG with no `viewBox`, so it neither grows nor shrinks. The reviewer measured 31px of chart cut off at a 430px viewport, unreachable because the page does not scroll horizontally, and 460px of chart in an 868px card at a wide one. Dashboard.md tells readers to do the opposite.

notes.text: The fixed pixel space is worth keeping for the ChartTooltip coordinate maths, which is what the comment in the demo is actually protecting. A viewBox with a percentage width gets both.

Closed with the note's suggestion, a `viewBox` at a percentage width, and the part the note did not cover. `ChartTooltip` takes container pixels rather than viewBox units, so a chart that scales moves its tooltip off the mark. A `ResizeObserver` gives the rendered width and the tooltip position is scaled by the same factor.

One thing was worth doing differently. Wrapping the drawn charts in `ChartFrame` first produced a bordered box hugging each chart, because the frame is a flex item in a centring parent. Letting it take the card's width is what makes it read as a panel rather than a stray box.
